summary.coverageNote: Reviewed the exact definitions and current labels for all 280 new-meaning rows across splits. Findings target training rows and compare relevant old TRAIN meanings. This is a policy-focused audit, not an accuracy estimate; no labels, splits, or data were changed.

findings.exactDefinition: To break apart into smaller pieces or particles.
findings.reason: This is a process verb whose endpoint is a visibly broken-apart condition. The old TRAIN sense “shatter” carries both action and state for the same break-into-pieces pattern; consider whether the disintegrated result is part of the required visual evidence.

counterparts.exactDefinition: To break suddenly into many sharp pieces.

primaryReview.assessment: Retain action for this experiment. A persistent aftermath alone is not a consistent reason to add state; review the old shatter co-label in a future policy revision.

findings.exactDefinition: To break or divide something into smaller pieces.
findings.reason: The definition explicitly includes division into smaller pieces, so an image of the resulting fragments may satisfy part of the selected meaning. Old TRAIN “shatter” is action+state for a very close event; the current action-only label may reflect a policy distinction that needs stating.

counterparts.exactDefinition: To break suddenly into many sharp pieces.

primaryReview.assessment: Verified near-parallel with shatter. This is a process/result policy conflict, not proof that this new action-only label is wrong.

findings.exactDefinition: To break into long, thin, sharp pieces.
findings.reason: The event produces long, thin, sharp pieces, making the resulting visible condition salient as well as the breakage event. Old TRAIN “shatter” is action+state; review whether this near-neighbor should share that treatment.

counterparts.exactDefinition: To break suddenly into many sharp pieces.

primaryReview.assessment: Verified unusually close definition to shatter, including sharp pieces. The differing state membership needs a consistent rule across both meanings.

findings.exactDefinition: To change from a liquid or gas into a solid.
findings.reason: Changing material into a solid is an event and yields a persistent solid condition. Old TRAIN “evaporate” is action+state for a phase change; clarify whether the endpoint condition merits state for both directions of phase change.

counterparts.exactDefinition: To change from liquid into vapor at a surface.

primaryReview.assessment: Phase-change precedent evaporate has state, while crystallize is action-only. Resolve the policy across all three rather than automatically adding state here.

findings.exactDefinition: For a material to deteriorate through chemical reaction with its surroundings.
findings.reason: The definition describes material deterioration through a chemical reaction, which may be visible both as an ongoing change and as a corroded surface. Old TRAIN “erode” is action+state for a closely related wear-away process; review whether chemical versus mechanical cause justifies the label difference.

counterparts.exactDefinition: To wear away gradually through water, wind, or friction.

primaryReview.assessment: Verified mismatch with erode for material deterioration. Chemical versus mechanical cause does not by itself explain different endpoint-state membership.

findings.exactDefinition: For tissue or another material to become hardened by deposits of calcium salts.
findings.reason: Calcification makes tissue or material harder through calcium deposits, so the resulting physical condition may be visible as well as the process. Old co-labeled transformation examples include “erode” and “inflate”; review whether this sense warrants action+state.

counterparts.exactDefinition: To fill with air or gas so that something expands.
To wear away gradually through water, wind, or friction.

primaryReview.assessment: Do not automatically add state: composition/history is not directly identifiable from many photos. Retain as a lower-confidence process/result policy question.

findings.exactDefinition: For a liquid, especially blood or protein, to thicken into a semisolid mass.
findings.reason: The definition includes a change of consistency ending in a semisolid mass, so a still image can show both the thickening event and its resulting condition. Old TRAIN phase-change “evaporate” is action+state; check whether that precedent applies.

counterparts.exactDefinition: To change from liquid into vapor at a surface.

primaryReview.assessment: Verified action-only versus action/state for other phase/consistency changes. A result-route policy is needed; the suggested label is not established gold.

findings.exactDefinition: For milk or a similar liquid to separate into lumps and thinner liquid.
findings.reason: The separation into lumps and thinner liquid is a visible resulting configuration as well as a change process. Compare old TRAIN “shatter,” which labels a break event and its visible aftermath action+state; review whether the same evidence logic applies.

counterparts.exactDefinition: To break suddenly into many sharp pieces.

primaryReview.assessment: Lumps and thinner liquid are visible results, but that does not automatically require a state category for a process. Review with other transformation verbs.

findings.exactDefinition: To crush or grind a solid into fine powder.
findings.reason: The definition ends with a solid reduced to fine powder, a visible condition distinct from the grinding event. Old TRAIN “shatter” co-labels an event and its pieces; review whether the endpoint is similarly meaningful here.

counterparts.exactDefinition: To break suddenly into many sharp pieces.

primaryReview.assessment: Verified difference from shatter. Fine powder versus sharp fragments does not by itself justify different result-state policy.

findings.exactDefinition: A raised road or path across low or wet ground.
findings.reason: A causeway is defined as a raised road/path crossing low or wet ground, so it can require evidence of the built structure and its spatial course. Old TRAIN bridge/overpass meanings carry entity+place+relation, while underpass is place-only; this looks like a boundary-policy question rather than a clear factual error.

counterparts.exactDefinition: A structure carrying a path over water or another obstacle.
A bridge carrying one road or path above another.
A passage that lets a road or path go beneath another route.

primaryReview.assessment: Verified structure/path/crossing overlap with bridge and overpass. Entity/place/relation annotation is not consistently specified across built routes.

findings.exactDefinition: A small roofed structure in a garden or park, open on the sides.
findings.reason: The selected meaning is explicitly a roofed structure, yet the label is place-only. Old TRAIN greenhouse and new TRAIN hothouse are entity+place for structures used as growing sites; review whether the same physical-structure evidence applies to a gazebo.

counterparts.exactDefinition: An enclosed structure with transparent walls for growing plants.

primaryReview.assessment: Verified explicit physical structure and setting. Entity+place is plausible under the greenhouse rule; record a proposed policy change, not a measured label error.

findings.exactDefinition: A building or place where eggs are incubated and young animals are raised.
findings.reason: The definition names a building or place where eggs are incubated. It may be place-only as an operating site, but its physical building form is also explicit, unlike a generic activity setting. Compare the entity+place greenhouse/hothouse treatment.

counterparts.exactDefinition: An enclosed structure with transparent walls for growing plants.

primaryReview.assessment: The definition permits a building OR a site, so place-only can be defensible. Reject any claim that an omitted entity label is definitely wrong.

findings.exactDefinition: A covered walkway around a courtyard, especially in a monastery.
findings.reason: The walkway’s defining layout is around a courtyard, an explicit spatial configuration between the walkway and the courtyard. Old TRAIN bridge/overpass senses include relation when the structure’s spatial arrangement is central; review whether “around” should trigger the same evidence label.

counterparts.exactDefinition: A structure carrying a path over water or another obstacle.
A bridge carrying one road or path above another.

primaryReview.assessment: The courtyard arrangement is definitionally central; relation membership is a substantive review candidate under the basement/bridge policy.

findings.exactDefinition: A low intermediate floor between two main floors of a building.
findings.reason: The definition identifies an intermediate floor by its position between two other floors. That vertical configuration is essential to the selected meaning. Old TRAIN underpass is place-only despite a “beneath another route” definition, so the relation boundary appears inconsistent and needs a policy decision.

counterparts.exactDefinition: A passage that lets a road or path go beneath another route.

primaryReview.assessment: Between-floor location is defining, comparable to basement/cellar position. This is a strong relation-boundary inconsistency candidate.

findings.exactDefinition: A barrier built offshore to reduce the force of waves at a harbor.
findings.reason: The definition calls this a built barrier offshore. A fixed structure can be an entity while its environmental role/location supports place; old TRAIN wall is entity-only and levee is place-only, leaving this analogous barrier ambiguous.

counterparts.exactDefinition: A vertical structure enclosing or dividing a space.
A raised bank built beside a river to prevent flooding.

primaryReview.assessment: An explicitly built barrier suggests entity evidence; place-only matches levee but conflicts with wall. The structural entity/place boundary needs clarification.

reviewType: AI semantic/policy review; not human-expert label accuracy
primaryConclusion: All 15 flags and cited counterparts independently inspected. They identify unresolved boundary policies; no ground-truth error rate is established. Training/evaluation labels remain frozen to isolate dropout.
